# Kinetograph

> A programmatic video engine with no browser in it. Write a video in TypeScript with Remotion's API, CSS, SVG,
> Canvas 2D, WebGL fragment shaders and Web Audio; Node runs the code; a Rust GPU compositor (an N-API addon on wgpu)
> draws every frame. `remotion` and `@remotion/*` imports resolve to Kinetograph's own implementation.

## Install

- `npm install kinetograph`, then run `npx kinetograph <command>` against the entry file of a Remotion-shaped project
- Source and issues: https://github.com/0xS4N4TG/kinetograph
- Licence: PolyForm Small Business 1.0.0 (free for individuals and companies under 100 people and $1M revenue a year)

## Why use it

- Renders without a browser: no Chrome to install, no display needed, so it runs on a server or in CI
- Measured 7.0x faster than Remotion on the same scene (S04, 89 frames at 1080p, Apple M4, `kinetograph bench`)
- A real Remotion project (papercut) renders all 988 of its frames natively
- Built for agents: `still`, `strip`, `inspect` and `lint` let a model check its own output before a person watches

## CLI

Every command takes `--json`. `npx kinetograph mcp` serves the same commands as an MCP server on stdio, one tool each.

- `npx kinetograph still <entry> <frame> -o frame.png`: one frame to a PNG
- `npx kinetograph strip <entry> -n 12 -o strip.png`: contact sheet of evenly spaced frames
- `npx kinetograph inspect <entry> --frame 60`: the scene graph at a frame (layers, bounds, resolved styles)
- `npx kinetograph lint <entry>`: overflowing text, off-canvas layers, missing fonts and assets, what cannot be drawn
- `npx kinetograph doctor <entry>`: what the engine cannot draw, and in which frames
- `npx kinetograph render <entry> -o out.mp4`: frames to a video with audio
- `npx kinetograph studio <entry>`: local preview, timeline, scene tree, props and render queue
- Also: `compositions`, `onion`, `check`, `bench`, `audio analyze`, `snapshot`, `effects`

## Native elements (from `@kinetograph/core`)

`<Scene3D>`, `<Camera3D>` (perspective or `type="orthographic"`), `<Mesh>`, `<Text3D>`, `<DirectionalLight>`,
`<GlslShader>` (GLSL ES fragment shaders with uniforms and textures), `<Canvas>` (a `draw(ctx)` Canvas 2D callback),
`<Layer>` (transforms, `motionBlur`), plus the effects listed by `kinetograph effects`.

## Determinism

`Date`, `Math.random`, timers and `requestAnimationFrame` follow the frame number. A frame is a pure function of
(project, frame); nothing reads the wall clock.

## Requirements

Node 22 or later, a GPU that wgpu supports (Metal on macOS), FFmpeg for `render`. No display needed.
